questions.q: What does blue-green deployment keep running side by side?
options: Two complete, independent environments — the current version and the new version, with traffic routed to only one at a time
One environment split into two separate KQL Databases
Two different Fabric Capacity SKUs simultaneously
Two copies of the same version for redundancy only
questions.explain: The new version (green) is fully live and tested before it ever receives real traffic, and rollback is just routing traffic back.

questions.q: Why is rollback in a blue-green deployment described as instant?
options: Pointing traffic back at the old environment (blue) means the old version is immediately serving again, with nothing to "undo" in the new version
Blue-green deployments never actually need to roll back
Rollback requires redeploying the entire pipeline from scratch
Instant rollback is only possible with canary deployments, not blue-green
questions.explain: The switch itself is just a routing change, which is why reversing it is equally simple and fast.

questions.q: How does a canary deployment differ from blue-green?
options: It routes a small percentage of real traffic to the new version first, expanding gradually if it looks correct, instead of switching everyone at once
It's identical to blue-green, just under a different name
Canary deployments never involve any real production traffic
Canary always switches 100% of traffic immediately, like blue-green
questions.explain: A bug in the new version affects only the small observed slice, not the whole system, before it's caught.

questions.q: Why might a canary deployment catch a bug that production-shaped test data (Lesson 44) can't?
options: It's tested against real production traffic, which occasionally reveals problems that even realistic test data genuinely can't surface
Canary deployments don't actually use any real data at all
Production-shaped test data is always sufficient and canary adds nothing
This scenario is impossible — test data always catches everything a canary would
questions.explain: Real traffic has quirks and edge cases that even well-designed test data can miss.

questions.q: When does blue-green suit a change better than canary, according to this lesson?
options: For a clean, all-or-nothing logic change, like migrating an Eventstream's storage destination, where a gradual rollout doesn't make sense
Blue-green is always strictly better than canary in every situation
Canary is always strictly better than blue-green in every situation
Blue-green only applies to Power BI reports, never Eventstreams
questions.explain: Canary suits changes where judging correctness gradually on real traffic is meaningful — some changes simply can't be half-migrated.
